create.name: Houston Zen Center
create.bio:
Houston Zen Center is a Soto Zen temple in the Heights district of Houston, Texas, in the line of Shunryu Suzuki Roshi and San Francisco Zen Center. It grew out of a sitting group that began meeting in a Unitarian church around 1988; Reb Anderson Roshi led retreats for the group from 1995, and his Dharma heir Konjin Gaelyn Godwin, who trained for eighteen years at San Francisco Zen Center and Tassajara, came to teach and settled in Houston in 2003, when the centre opened. Since 2007 it has occupied a large 1918 Craftsman house on Heights Boulevard, and Godwin was installed as abbot in 2012. A number of priests and lay teachers she has trained now teach alongside her.

Daily zazen is free and open to anyone, in the zendo or through the Zoom Zendo, and the Sunday programme adds a Dharma talk. There is a monthly hour of instruction for newcomers, and courses for all levels on Zen texts, history and practice, along with groups in Spanish, for queer practitioners and for those in recovery. An hour west of the city, near Chappell Hill, its rural Auspicious Cloud retreat land hosts sesshin and longer retreats. Membership dues keep the doors open, and scholarships mean cost need not keep anyone away.

courses.title: Rohatsu Sesshin 2026
courses.description: The centre's yearly five-day intensive sitting retreat in early December, held at Auspicious Cloud Zen Retreat Center and led by Abbot Gaelyn Godwin with priest Tim Schorre. Open to those who have sat at least one one-day sesshin; a weekend-only option is offered.
courses.price: $500 for the entire sesshin; HZC Member $300; Friday-Sunday $300 / $200 for members

courses.title: Introduction to Zen Meditation - Series of 5 classes
courses.description: A five-week in-person beginners' course with Gaelyn Godwin and Royce Johnson covering basic Zen outlook, sitting, standing, walking and lying-down meditation, and bringing practice into ordinary days. Sitting time builds from ten to thirty minutes.

courses.title: Mind to Mind: The History and Transmission of Zen
courses.description: Five Tuesday evening classes with Koun Matthew Brownlie tracing Zen from the Buddha through the Chinese Chan masters to Japan, Korea, Vietnam and the West. In person or on Zoom.

courses.title: The Holy Upheaval: The Teaching of Vimalakirti
courses.description: A six-class reading of the Vimalakirti Sutra with senior member Sanran Maite Leal, exploring how the text joins everyday and ultimate reality. In person or on Zoom.

free_resources.title: Zoom Zendo
free_resources.description: Links for joining the centre's daily zazen and weekend programme remotely. Sitting periods are free and open to everyone.

free_resources.title: Dharma Talks
free_resources.description: Upcoming and recorded Sunday Dharma talks by the abbot, the centre's priests and visiting teachers.
